title: Real Clifford Modules, KO Theory, and ABS Orientations

items.title: Real and quaternionic bundle K-groups
items.statement: For a finite CW complex X, KO^0(X) is the Grothendieck group of isomorphism classes of finite-rank real vector bundles under direct sum. KSp^0(X) is the Grothendieck group of finite-rank right-H vector bundles and H-linear isomorphisms. Pullback acts on both groups. Tensoring a real bundle with a right-H bundle gives the KO^0(X)-module structure on KSp^0(X); no internal KSp product is needed here.

items.title: Reduced and relative real K-theory and compact support
items.statement: For a based finite CW complex (X,x0), define reduced KO^0 by ker(KO^0(X)→KO^0(x0)). For a finite CW pair A⊂X, define KO^0(X,A)=reduced KO^0(X/A); write KO_c^0(V)=reduced KO^0(Th(V)) for a finite-rank Euclidean bundle V, and define KO^(−j)(X,A)=reduced KO^0(Σ^j(X/A)) for j≥0. The basepoint and quotient conventions are part of the definition.

items.title: Given Spin and Spin-c structures and their spinor bundles
items.statement: Let V→X be an oriented Euclidean real vector bundle of rank n, with oriented frame bundle P_SO(V). Use Spin(n)=Spin_full(ℝⁿ,−‖·‖²), the full even subgroup of the negative-square Pin group, and its standard twisted-Clifford homomorphism λ_n:Spin(n)→SO(n). A Spin structure on V is a principal Spin(n)-bundle P with a Spin(n)-equivariant two-fold map P→P_SO(V) covering the identity on X and compatible with λ_n. A Spin^c structure is a principal Spin^c(n) lift of P_SO(V), where Spin^c(n)=(Spin(n)×U(1))/⟨(−1,−1)⟩. A spinor bundle is the associated bundle for the specified real Clifford representation; a Spin^c spinor bundle uses the specified complex representation and its U(1) weight. These are given structures; this definition asserts no existence criterion.

items.title: Real graded Clifford-module bundles and their Grothendieck groups
items.statement: Let V→X be a finite-rank Euclidean real vector bundle and put C(V)=Cl(V,−⟨·,·⟩), so each vector v acts with square −‖v‖². A real graded C(V)-module bundle is a finite-rank real vector bundle Λ=Λ^0⊕Λ^1 with a continuous fiberwise unital action preserving the grading and satisfying the Clifford relations. Let M(V) be the Grothendieck group of their isomorphism classes under direct sum.

items.title: Clifford-module restriction cokernels A_n
items.statement: For n≥0 put C_n=Cl(ℝ^n,−‖·‖²). Let M_n be the Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional real Z/2-graded left C_n-modules and let r_n:M_{n+1}→M_n be restriction along the standard inclusion of the first n Clifford generators. Define A_n=coker(r_n). For n=0 the grading is retained, so M_0≅Z⊕Z from even and odd dimensions; no parity type is identified with a volume-element eigenspace.

items.title: A numerated real bundle embeds in a finite trivial bundle
items.statement: Let X be compact Hausdorff and let E→X be a rank-r real vector bundle with a finite linear trivializing cover (U_i,φ_i) and a subordinate finite partition of unity (ρ_i). Then some N and a bundle F→X satisfy E⊕F≅X×ℝ^N. The embedding and orthogonal complement construction uses only the supplied finite numeration.

items.title: Finite-CW real bundles have orthogonal complements under AC
items.statement: Assume AC. If X is a finite CW complex and E→X is any finite-rank real vector bundle, then E is isomorphic to a subbundle of a finite trivial bundle and has an orthogonal vector-bundle complement.

items.title: Finite-CW relative KO triples and homotopy invariance
items.statement: For finite CW pairs, relative KO classes can be represented by triples of real bundles and an isomorphism over the subspace, modulo stabilization and homotopy. Pullback along homotopic maps gives the same KO class, with the exact finite-CW hypotheses and any reused axiom assumptions stated explicitly.

items.title: Suspension, exactness, and products in relative KO
items.statement: For finite CW pairs (X,A), the relative KO groups defined by the quotient satisfy the cofiber long exact sequence, are compatible with suspension, and have the external and internal products induced by bundle tensor product. State and prove the pair and basepoint conventions used by the Clifford–Thom map.

items.title: Orthogonal Clifford families and centriole spaces
items.statement: Let p be even and define SO(p)={J∈M_p(ℝ):JᵀJ=I, det J=1}. Its trace metric is the left-invariant Riemannian metric whose inner product at the identity is ⟨A,B⟩=−(1/p)tr(AB) for skew-symmetric A,B; at J its value on tangent vectors JA,JB is the same. An orthogonal negative-square Clifford family of length l is a list J₁,…,J_l∈SO(p) with J_i²=−I and J_iJ_j=−J_jJ for i≠j, equivalently a representation of C_l=Cl(ℝ^l,−‖·‖²) by these matrices. For a Riemannian manifold P and points x,y, its midpoint set is {γ(1/2): γ:[0,1]→P is a length-minimizing geodesic from x to y}; a centriole is a connected component of such a midpoint set. Put P₀=SO(p), J₀=I, and for j≥1 define P̂_j={J∈SO(p):J²=−I and JJ_i=−J_iJ for i<j}; let P_j be the connected component of P̂_j containing J_j. A compatible family also satisfies J_j∈P_(j−1). The geometric midpoint interpretation of this algebraic component is the claim of the next lemma.

items.title: Clifford centrioles and geodesic tangent conditions
items.statement: For p even, the trace metric, and a compatible orthogonal Clifford family J₁,…,J_l as defined in [[def-orthogonal-clifford-families-and-centrioles]], let M_j be the midpoint set in P_(j−1) between J_(j−1) and −J_(j−1), with J₀=I. The component of M_j containing J_j is exactly the component P_j of the algebraic locus P̂_j. Each P_j is totally geodesic. For a skew-symmetric matrix A, the curve t↦exp(tA)J_j lies in P_j for every real t exactly when A anticommutes with J_j and commutes with each J_i for i<j.

items.title: Relative path-shortening connectivity from index bounds
items.statement: Let P be a compact Riemannian manifold, o,p∈P, and Ω_*(o,p) a fixed path component of the H¹ path space of paths from o to p. Let Ω_*^0 be the subset of length-minimizing geodesics in that component. The energy is E(γ)=∫₀¹‖γ′(t)‖²dt; a geodesic is nonminimal if it does not minimize length, and its Morse index is the maximal dimension of a subspace of endpoint-vanishing variation fields on which the second variation of E is negative definite. If every nonminimal critical geodesic in Ω_* has Morse index at least d+1, then Ω_*^0→Ω_* is d-connected: for every finite CW pair (K,A) of dimension at most d, every map K→Ω_* carrying A into Ω_*^0 is homotopic relative to A to a map with all of K in Ω_*^0. The exact finite-dimensional polygon approximation and relative Morse argument are not supplied by the cited source and remain required locally.

items.title: Real Clifford block-rotation index bounds
items.statement: Let J₁,…,J_l be the family in [[def-orthogonal-clifford-families-and-centrioles]], let γ be a nonminimal geodesic in P_l, and let ind(γ) be the Morse index of its energy on endpoint-fixed variation fields. Decompose ℝ^p into minimal mutually orthogonal subspaces invariant under the Clifford family and the geodesic generator; each such block is a finite-dimensional Clifford module. Write s_q for the real dimension of an irreducible C_q-module, fixed by the exact real Clifford classification. A two-block rotation is the variation generated by the skew operator with matrix blocks (0,−I; I,0) on two isomorphic invariant blocks and zero on the others; different counted pairs must yield linearly independent directions for the index form. If l is not congruent to 2 modulo 4, prove the safe lower bound ind(γ)≥p/s_(l+1)−1, retaining one unit of slack when using it to prove ind(γ)>d. If l=4m−2, the loop γ(t)J_l⁻¹ lies in U(p/2); define its winding w as the winding number of its complex determinant. In this residue class prove that p−4|w|≥4d s_l implies ind(γ)>d. The strictness gap in the source's Proposition 5.4 remains unresolved.

items.title: Iterated suspension and winding control
items.statement: Let k=4m−1 and let ρ:C_k→SO(p) be a negative-square orthogonal representation with generators J₁,…,J_k. Call ρ positive when J_k=J₁⋯J_(k−1). For l=k−1, identify P_l with its unitary image J↦JJ_l⁻¹ in U(p/2). For a based loop ω:S¹→P_l, define its winding η(ω) as the winding number of det_C(ωJ_l⁻¹):S¹→S¹. The geodesic suspension Σ_J maps a based map into P_(j+1) to the map one sphere dimension higher into P_j by using the shortest geodesics from J_j to −J_j along the suspension coordinate. Iterating these maps gives θ:Map_*(S¹,P_(k−1))→Map_*(S^k,SO(p)); define the stable winding label on the image by η_s∘θ=η and extend it over stabilized block sums. Prove that this is well-defined and invariant under stabilization, that prior extendibility forces zero winding in the l=4m−2 residue, and that the terminal winding component is preserved. The positivity convention, suspension connectivity and stabilization-invariance proof are part of the obligation.

items.title: Affine Clifford–Hopf maps are highly connected
items.statement: Let k=4m−1, d≥1, and ρ:C_k→SO(p) be positive in the convention of [[lem-iterated-suspension-and-winding-control-for-clifford-families]]. Let s_k be the real dimension of an irreducible C_k-module and let η be the stable winding label. The Clifford Hopf map is μ_ρ:S^k=S(ℝ⊕ℝ^k)→SO(p), μ_ρ(x₀,…,x_k)=x₀I+∑_(i=1)^k x_iJ_i. Let i=J₁⋯J_(k−2), the specified complex structure on the invariant blocks, and write ℂ-dimension with respect to i. An affine Hopf map of winding η is the block map I on an invariant complement L₀ and μ_(ρ|L₁) on an invariant C_k-submodule L₁ with dim_ℂ(L₁)=η. For p≥p₀(d) and s_k d≤η≤p/4, the inclusion of these affine Hopf maps into the stable-winding-η component Map_*(S^k,SO(p))_η is d-connected in the finite-CW relative sense defined in [[lem-relative-path-shortening-connectivity]].

items.title: Volume chirality and Clifford–Hopf clutching
items.statement: Let V→X be an oriented Euclidean real vector bundle of rank n=4m>0 and let Λ=Λ⁰⊕Λ¹ be a real graded C(V)-module bundle, where C(V)=Cl(V,−⟨·,·⟩). In an oriented orthonormal frame (e₁,…,eₙ) set ω=c(e₁)…c(eₙ). Then ω is frame-independent, has square 1, preserves grading, and its eigenspaces Λ⁺ and Λ⁻ are graded subbundles interchanged by multiplication by every unit vector v. Gluing the pullbacks of Λ⁺ and Λ⁻ over the two disk halves of S(ℝ⊕V) by c(v):Λ⁺→Λ⁻ along S(V) defines the associated Clifford–Hopf clutching bundle. Its relative clutching triple is (Λ⁺,c(v),Λ⁻); the volume eigensplitting is not the parity grading or the even/odd-word splitting of the regular algebra.

items.title: Stable Clifford–Hopf decomposition over sphere bundles
items.statement: Let X be a finite CW complex and V→X an oriented Euclidean bundle of rank n=4m>0. Put V̂=S(ℝ⊕V), with projection π and pole sections s_±(x)=(±1,0). For a C(V)-module bundle Λ, let H(V,Λ) be the sphere-bundle clutching bundle of [[lem-volume-chirality-and-clifford-hopf-clutching]]. The regular Clifford–Hopf bundle means H(V,C(V)) for the regular graded module. Every real vector bundle over V̂ becomes, after adding finitely many trivial bundles and regular Clifford–Hopf bundles, a direct sum π^*E₀⊕H(V,Λ), where E₀ is a real bundle on X and Λ is a graded C(V)-module bundle. The local proof must preserve the rank, winding, finite-CW and stabilization hypotheses during cell induction.

items.title: Uniqueness of the stable Clifford–Hopf decomposition
items.statement: Under the finite-CW and rank hypotheses of [[thm-stable-clifford-hopf-decomposition-over-sphere-bundles]], suppose π^*E₀⊕H(V,Λ) and π^*E₁⊕H(V,Μ) become isomorphic after adding trivial real bundles and regular Clifford–Hopf bundles. Here module-bundle stable isomorphism means that Λ and Μ become isomorphic after adding finite direct sums of the regular graded C(V)-module. Then E₀ and E₁ are stably isomorphic over X, and Λ and Μ are stably isomorphic as graded C(V)-module bundles. The local proof must use the explicit block-rotation estimate and the relative cell argument over X×I, whose dimension is dim X+1.

items.title: Real Clifford–Thom isomorphism
items.statement: For a finite CW complex X and oriented Euclidean bundle V→X of rank n=4m≥0, let M(V) be the Grothendieck group of graded real C(V)-module bundles and KO_c^0(V)=\\widetilde{KO}^0(Th(V)). Define Φ_V:M(V)→KO_c^0(V) by sending [Λ] to the relative class of the volume-eigenspace clutching triple (Λ^+,c(v),Λ^−) from [[lem-volume-chirality-and-clifford-hopf-clutching]], equivalently the associated bundle H(V,Λ) minus the pullback of its plus eigenspace along the north-pole section. Prove Φ_V is an isomorphism, identify the kernel before quotienting, and include the rank-zero case with its basepoint convention.

items.title: Real and quaternionic spinor Morita evaluation
items.statement: For a given Spin structure and rank-8m or rank-(8m+4) Euclidean bundle V, let Σ be the specified irreducible graded real Clifford spinor bundle and let D=ℝ in rank 8m and D=ℍ in rank 8m+4. In the quaternionic case take the commuting right-H action on Σ and define the right action on Hom_C(V)(Σ,Λ) by (f·q)(s)=f(s\\bar q); give Σ the corresponding left-H action q·s=s\\bar q. Thus Hom_C(V)(Σ,Λ)⊗_HΣ is a balanced tensor product. Prove the evaluation map f⊗s↦f(s) is a bundle isomorphism, with the analogous real tensor product in the rank-8m case. The commutant type and this exact conjugation convention must be checked from the real/graded Clifford classification.

items.title: Real spin Thom classes in ranks divisible by eight and four
items.statement: For a given Spin bundle V over a finite CW base, multiplication by its real spinor Hopf class defines a map KO^0(X)→\\widetilde{KO}^0(Th(V)) when rank(V)=8m and a map KSp^0(X)→\\widetilde{KO}^0(Th(V)) when rank(V)=8m+4. In the first case the class is represented by the real spinor module; in the second it is represented by the quaternionic spinor module with the right-H convention of [[lem-real-and-quaternionic-spinor-module-morita-evaluation]]. Prove both maps are natural isomorphisms and compatible with direct sums; retain the two source theories as distinct branches.

items.title: Real Bott periodicity from the rank-eight Clifford–Thom map
items.statement: Let β∈\\widetilde{KO}^0(S^8) be the rank-eight real spinor Hopf class of the trivial bundle. For every finite CW complex X, external product with β gives KO^0(X)→\\widetilde{KO}^0(X_+∧S^8). Prove this map is an isomorphism, derive reduced and relative forms via the section/wedge split exact sequence, extend to every suspended degree, and prove multiplicativity. This is the local real Bott theorem and is not inferred from complexification.

items.title: Real and symplectic clutching groups in low degrees
items.statement: Write O=colim_n O(n) and Sp=colim_r Sp(r) under standard block inclusions. Clutching over S^n identifies \\widetilde{KO}^0(S^n) with π_(n−1)(O) and \\widetilde{KSp}^0(S^n) with π_(n−1)(Sp) in the stable range. Compute KO^(−1)(pt)=π₀(O)=ℤ/2, KO^(−2)(pt)=π₁(O)=ℤ/2, KO^(−3)(pt)=π₂(O)=0 and KSp^(−j)(pt)=π_(j−1)(Sp)=0 for j=1,2,3 from the orthogonal and symplectic sphere fibrations, the SO(3) double cover, and the stated low homotopy suppliers.

items.title: The real KO coefficient table and eightfold periodicity
items.statement: For n=0,…,7, the groups KO^(−n)(pt) are ℤ,ℤ/2,ℤ/2,0,ℤ,0,0,0 in that order. Multiplication by the rank-eight class β gives KO^(−n)(pt)≅KO^(−n−8)(pt) in every degree. Prove the low rows from the local clutching computation and the rank-four Spin/KSp boundary; extend all remaining degrees only through the locally proved rank-eight real Bott theorem.

items.title: The ABS Clifford cokernel and symbol map
items.statement: For C_n=Cl(ℝ^n,−‖·‖²), a finite-dimensional graded real module M=M^0⊕M^1 determines the ABS symbol triple (π^*M^0,π^*M^1,c(v)) on the disk/sphere pair of ℝ^n: over a nonzero vector v, Clifford multiplication c(v) is an isomorphism because c(v)^2=−‖v‖²I. Its relative KO class is the candidate symbol. The associated theorem is assigned to establish that the symbol vanishes on restrictions from C_(n+1), descends to A_n, and is an isomorphism.

items.title: Graded C_n modules and ungraded C_(n−1) modules
items.statement: For n≥1, taking the even part is an equivalence from finite-dimensional graded C_n-modules to finite-dimensional ungraded C_(n−1)-modules, where C_n=Cl(ℝⁿ,−‖·‖²). An inverse is induction from the even subalgebra. For n=0, C_0 is purely even and the even-part functor loses odd-only modules, so retain both parity types and treat the restriction cokernel separately.

items.title: Restriction matrices for real Clifford modules
items.statement: For C_n=Cl(ℝ^n,−‖·‖²), let M_n be the Grothendieck group of finite-dimensional graded real C_n-modules and r_n:M_(n+1)→M_n restriction along the first n generators. Using the exact real Clifford and graded-module tables, compute each r_n as an integer matrix in the classified irreducible-module bases and compute A_n=coker(r_n). Retain M_0=ℤ⊕ℤ with its even/odd parity basis. The output table must give every residue row n=0,…,7 and the periodic continuation, with the sign/index shift translated from the plus-square convention.

items.title: The ABS symbol identifies Clifford cokernels with KO coefficients
items.statement: For C_n=Cl(ℝ^n,−‖·‖²), define α_n on a graded module M=M^0⊕M^1 by the relative symbol triple (π^*M^0,π^*M^1,c(v)) over the disk/sphere pair, with section subtraction and the map to \\widetilde{KO}^0(S^n). Prove that this symbol vanishes on restrictions from M_(n+1), so factors through A_n=coker(r_n), and that the induced α_n:A_n→KO^(−n)(pt) is an isomorphism. Identify the kernel before quotienting, verify n=0,1,2,4,8, and prove multiplicativity under the graded tensor product. The ABS comparison theorem that imports real periodicity is not a local proof.

items.title: Real Spin KO Thom orientation in all ranks and degrees
items.statement: For a given Spin real vector bundle V of rank r over a finite CW pair (X,A), the real spinor symbol defines a degree-shifted map KO^j(X,A)→KO^(j−r)(Th(V)) in every integer degree j. Construct the map by adding a trivial real bundle to reach rank divisible by eight, applying the local rank-eight Spin Thom theorem, and desuspending. Prove independence of stabilization, naturality and direct-sum/product compatibility. If r≡4 mod 8, use KSp as the unshifted source before applying the degree shift.

items.title: Complex Spin-c Thom orientation in even rank
items.statement: For a given Spin^c bundle V of even rank over a finite CW pair, the complex graded spinor bundle gives the relative symbol (S^+,S^−,c(v)) and a class in reduced/relative complex K-theory. Multiplication by this class defines a natural KU Thom map in every degree. Prove equivariance for Spin^c(n)=(Spin(n)×U(1))/⟨(−1,−1)⟩, including the U(1) weight, identify the fiber symbol with the complex Bott generator using the graded tensor model, and give the complete finite-CW induction and direct-sum proof.

items.title: Finite-dimensional gapped free Hamiltonians and stable equivalence
items.statement: A finite-dimensional free-fermion Hamiltonian is a self-adjoint matrix on a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. It is gapped at zero if 0 is not in its spectrum. A symmetry class is specified by named unitary and antiunitary operators and exact commutation, anticommutation and square relations with H. Stable equivalence means gap-preserving homotopy after direct sum with fixed reference trivial bands; phases are differences of stabilized systems, not absolute modules.

items.title: Spectral flattening preserves gaps and symmetry relations
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional self-adjoint gapped Hamiltonian H, define sign(H) by its spectral decomposition: it is +1 on positive eigenspaces and −1 on negative eigenspaces. The path H_t=(1−t)H+t sign(H) is continuous, remains gapped, and preserves every unitary or antiunitary symmetry relation S H S⁻¹=σH with σ∈{+1,−1}. At t=1 it is a self-adjoint involution.

items.title: Antiunitary AZ symmetry classes give Clifford extension problems
items.statement: In the finite-dimensional stable gapped free model, let T be antiunitary time reversal with THT⁻¹=H and T²=±1, and let C be antiunitary particle-hole symmetry with C H C⁻¹=−H and C²=±1. If both are present, Γ=TC is unitary and anticommutes with H; class A has neither antiunitary constraint and class AIII has Γ alone. After the spectral flattening of [[lem-spectral-flattening-preserves-gap-and-symmetries]], derive the real-linear Clifford generators and their squares for AI (+,+ absent C), BDI (+,+), D (C²=+), DIII (T²=−, C²=+), AII (T²=− absent C), CII (−,−), C (C²=−), CI (+,−), and the two complex classes A/AIII. The ordered eight real indices and mass-generator convention must follow from these explicit relations.

items.title: Tenfold real and complex Clifford-extension table
items.statement: For the specified finite-dimensional stable Dirac-mass extension problem with d fixed negative-square gamma generators and one flattened mass, the strong d-dimensional group at real index q is KO^(−(q−d))(pt); the complex analogue for indices 0 and 1 is KU^(−(q−d))(pt). Prove the explicit sign-changing Morita equivalence Cl_(p+1,q+1)≅M₂(Cl_(p,q)), identify all real residues q=0,…,7 and complex residues q=0,1, and state the class-by-dimension table. The result concerns only this finite stable free mass model; it gives no weak lattice, arbitrary-disorder, or interaction-stable classification.

title: Real Clifford Modules, KO Theory, and ABS Orientations: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: The zero-dimensional Clifford cokernel is Z
items.statement: With the parity grading retained, M_0=Z⊕Z and restriction from C_1 identifies its image with the diagonal subgroup generated by (1,1). Thus A_0≅Z via even dimension minus odd dimension.

items.title: Low-dimensional real Clifford signatures
items.statement: Under the positive-square-first convention, the real algebras Cl_(1,0), Cl_(0,1), Cl_(2,0), Cl_(1,1), and Cl_(0,2) are respectively R⊕R, C, M_2(R), M_2(R), and H.

items.title: The low-degree real KO coefficient table
items.statement: The coefficients in degrees 0 through 7 are Z, Z/2, Z/2, 0, Z, 0, 0, 0, respectively; the degree-four row is the quaternionic rank-four boundary case and the degree-eight class is the real Bott generator.

items.title: Changing the Clifford square sign changes the low-rank algebra
items.statement: The assertion that the one-generator real Clifford algebras for v²=+1 and v²=−1 are isomorphic is false: the former is R⊕R and the latter is C.

items.title: Rank four mod eight has KSp as the unshifted source
items.statement: For a Spin bundle of rank 8m+4, the source of the unshifted real Thom map is KSp(X); the real spinor is quaternionic, and the rank-eight KO statement must not be used in this residue class.

items.title: The tangent bundle of RP² is not Spin
items.statement: The tangent bundle of RP² is nonorientable, so it cannot be supplied with a Spin structure; its characteristic-class boundary is w₁(T RP²)≠0.

items.title: A zero-dimensional class-A flattened Hamiltonian
items.statement: On $\mathbb C^2$, let $H=\operatorname{diag}(-1,+1)$. It is already flattened, with occupied projection $P=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$ onto its negative eigenspace. With the zero-band reference and the rank-difference convention $\nu(H)=\dim E_{<0}(H)-\dim E_{<0}(H_{\rm ref})$, the occupied-rank index is $\nu(H)=1$.

items.title: A one-dimensional BDI Dirac-mass extension
items.statement: In the declared BDI finite Dirac-mass convention, take q=1 and d=1. Exhibit the real gamma and symmetry generators, verify their squares and anticommutation relations, and compute an explicit one-parameter integer-valued family whose class is the generator of KO^0(pt)=ℤ under the extension theorem. The family must be written as finite matrices and its invariant evaluated directly.

items.title: Strong, weak, and interaction-stability scope
items.statement: The A-page table concerns strong invariants of the finite-dimensional stable Dirac-mass extension problem. Weak invariants require additional lattice or torus hypotheses, and the free-fermion table does not assert general interaction stability or a classification of every disordered system.
